title: Where state lives in each tool
summary: The cloud keeps state for native tools, while you keep it for Terraform.

steps.n: The engineer sends a template and CloudFormation records it as a stack.
The service creates the resources and tracks them itself, so no state file is needed.
With Terraform the engineer plans and applies from their own machine or pipeline.
Terraform writes what it created to a state file in a backend that the team must protect.
Terraform calls the same cloud APIs to build the resources.
If the state file is corrupted, Terraform no longer knows what it owns until it is repaired.

title: Deploying a CloudFormation stack
summary: Validation, deploy and events show the path from file to resources.

steps.n: The engineer runs validate-template to catch syntax errors early.
The deploy command uploads the template with parameter values.
CloudFormation reads the template and builds a plan of resources and dependencies.
It creates resources in dependency order, such as the role before the function.
Each resource status is reported as an event the CLI prints.
The stack reaches CREATE_COMPLETE and outputs become available.

title: Resolving a template at deploy time
summary: Parameters, mappings and conditions turn one template into an environment.

steps.n: The deployer passes Env=prod as a parameter.
FindInMap uses Env to read the instance type m5.large from the mapping.
The condition IsProd becomes true because Env equals prod.
The alarm resource guarded by IsProd is created.
The server resource receives the looked-up instance type.
With Env=dev the alarm is skipped and a smaller instance is used from the same file.

title: Reading a change set before updating
summary: The preview shows replacement before data is lost.

steps.n: The engineer proposes the new template without applying it.
CloudFormation compares the new template to the running stack.
The change set lists Modify Database with Replacement True.
The reviewer sees that replacement would delete the database and asks for a snapshot policy.
The engineer adds UpdateReplacePolicy Snapshot and creates a new change set.
The reviewer approves, the change set is executed and the stack updates safely.

title: A StackSet rollout
summary: One template reaches many accounts with a stop on failure.

steps.n: The admin defines a baseline role template and the target accounts.
The first batch deploys the stack to account A.
Account B receives the stack in the same batch within the concurrency limit.
Account B reports a failure because a role name already exists.
The tolerance of one failure is reached, so the rollout stops before reaching more accounts.
The admin fixes the conflict and resumes the operation.

title: Drift detection finds a manual change
summary: A console edit is found and reconciled through code.

steps.n: An engineer opens a security group port in the console during an incident.
The real security group now differs from the template.
A scheduled drift detection compares actual properties with the template.
The report shows the expected and actual values for the changed rule.
The team decides the rule is not needed and re-applies the stack.
The resource matches the template again and the manual change is gone.

title: From Bicep file to Azure resources
summary: The compiler checks the file and Resource Manager creates resources.

steps.n: The engineer writes parameters, a storage account resource and an output.
The Bicep compiler checks types and produces an ARM template.
The ARM template and parameters are sent to Azure Resource Manager.
Resource Manager reads references and decides which resources come first.
The storage account is created inside the resource group.
The blob endpoint is returned as a deployment output.

title: A module with a loop
summary: One module creates a subnet for each name in a list.

steps.n: main.bicep passes the vnet name and a list of subnet names.
The module declares the virtual network first.
A for expression creates one subnet resource for each name.
Each subnet is created as a child of the vnet with its own address range.
The module returns the vnet id for other modules to use.
Adding one more name to the list creates one more subnet and leaves the others untouched.

title: What-if prevents a surprise delete
summary: The preview exposes a delete that complete mode would perform.

steps.n: The pipeline runs what-if for the pull request before any deployment.
The preview compares the template with the current resource group contents.
It lists a Create, a Modify and a Delete for a virtual machine.
The reviewer notices the template was run in complete mode with a partial file.
The pipeline is switched to incremental mode and the template is completed.
The deployment now adds and updates resources without deleting the VM.

title: A pipeline using a federated identity
summary: No secret is stored because a short-lived token is exchanged.

steps.n: The pipeline job starts and requests an OIDC token from the CI provider.
The token states the repository, branch and environment of the job.
The pipeline presents it to the cloud identity service.
The cloud checks that the token matches the rule allowing only the main branch to deploy.
The cloud returns credentials that expire in about an hour.
The pipeline deploys with these credentials, and nothing secret was ever stored.

title: Checks before a template merges
summary: Lint, policy and preview run in a fixed order.

steps.n: The developer pushes a template change and CI starts.
cfn-lint checks the syntax and property names and reports no errors.
cfn-guard evaluates the rule that security groups must not allow SSH from anywhere.
The check reports the offending rule and its location.
The pull request cannot merge until the source range is narrowed.
The developer fixes the rule, all checks pass and the preview is attached for review.

title: Failure and recovery: a stack create fails
summary: The first failed event holds the real reason.

steps.n: The engineer deploys a stack and sees a vague message that creation failed.
One bucket is rejected because its name is already used in another account.
CloudFormation cancels the remaining resources and begins to roll back.
The engineer lists stack events and looks at the earliest failure, not the last.
The event says the bucket name already exists, which explains all the later cancellations.
A stack stuck in ROLLBACK_COMPLETE cannot be updated, so it is deleted.
The template now lets CloudFormation generate the name and the deploy is repeated.
CloudTrail confirms the pipeline role made the calls, with no permission problems.

title: Failure and recovery: replacement deletes a database
summary: A small change replaced a database and the team recovers from a snapshot.

steps.n: The engineer changes a database property and runs the update directly.
The property requires replacement, so a new empty database is created.
The old database is deleted when the update completes.
The application starts and reports that all tables are empty.
The engineer finds the last automated snapshot from earlier that day.
A new database is restored from the snapshot and the application is pointed at it.
UpdateReplacePolicy Snapshot, DeletionPolicy and a change set review step are added.
Future replacements keep a snapshot and are reviewed before they run.
